newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK-based IPOs seen challenged by China issues.
newsitem.headline: HK-based IPOs seen challenged by China issues.

text.p: Hong Kong firms hoping to list on the local stock exchange face increasing competition for funds from China-related companies, which are considered more appealing investments, analysts said.

Weaker fundamentals and unexciting businesses mean Hong Kong's new listings are unlikely to enjoy the level of interest shown in Glorious Sun Enterprise Ltd's 250 million share initial public offering which was 236 times subscribed.

"Companies selling China concepts have their fans and are gaining attention. For others, it seems harder to attract market interest," said Patrick Chia, research manager at China Everbright Research, on Friday.
Analysts said Glorious Sun -- which makes and sells casual wear mainly in China -- was well sought after because it stood to benefit from the improving Chinese economy.

"Glorious Sun is successful because of its concept of tapping the potentially huge Chinese retail market which shows signs of picking up, especially after China lowered its interest rate," said Carol Lai, research manager at Amsteel Securities.
"The retail sector is still gloomy in Hong Kong," she said.
More than 20 local and state-owned Chinese enterprises are expected to seek listings in Hong Kong by the end of 1996.
Analysts said local issue sizes were expected to be small at about HK$100 million ($12.8 million) on average.
"A subscription of 50 to 60 times will be the maximum (for the local listings) in view of their size and industries," said Michael Ng, analyst from ASG Brokerage.
They are tapping the market at the same time as a large number of China-related companies are pouring into Hong Kong in search of funds ahead of the 1997 handover to China.
"Infrastructure stocks are expected to flood the market. Apart from new H-share listings, many local companies are expected to spin off infrastructure businesses," said Chia.
H-shares are stocks of China-incorporated companies listed in Hong Kong.
New listings in the pipeline include bus operator Kwoon Chung Bus Holdings Ltd which is launching a 59 million share offering at HK$1.80 each from September 13-18.
The company runs buses on Hong Kong's rural but rapidly developing Lantau Island and plans to use the funds to expand into major Chinese cities.
Analysts said they expected only a fair response from investors who perceive the company as rather unexciting.
Local office property investor and developer Wah Tak Fung Holdings Ltd is expected to issue 138 million new shares at HK$1.88 each in a flotation later in September.
Chia said an oversupply of office space in the territory was expected to dampen the response to the issue.

Among other expected issues are locally-based Mirabell Footwear Ltd, which is expected to raise about HK$100 million, Taiwan sports shoemaker Pegasus Group, seen raising HK$150 million, and Hong Kong household appliances supplier Alpha Appliances Ltd, which is expected to raise HK$100 million.

Hong Kong-based SmarTone Mobile Communications Ltd is planning to raise about HK$2.00 billion and China-backed China Resources Enterprise Ltd unit China Resources Beijing Land Ltd is expected to list later this year.

Analysts said Beijing-controlled Hong Kong satellite owner and operator APT Satellite Co Ltd should attract overseas interest. It is expected to raise US$200 to US$300 million through a dual listing in Hong Kong and the United States. (US$1 = HK$7.8) -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6370
